target.question:
I am working with a few forms in our ServiceNow portal. Create Change Request vs Problem vs Incident vs Hardware vs User. Among create-request, problem, incident, hardware, and user forms, how many forms have subtabs on the page, in addition to the field-entering section? Answer in English (zero/one/two/three/four/five)

Mark your final answer (should be one or more short phrases) in \boxed{}.

results.answer:
Going by what's recorded about the portal, **three** of the five forms have subtabs below the field-entry section:

- **Create Change Request** (change_request.do) has tabs: Planning (Justification, Implementation plan, Test plan and similar), Schedule (Planned start and end dates) and Closure Information (Close code, Close notes).
- **Incident** (incident.do) has tabs: Notes, Related Records and Resolution Information. This applies to the standard view only. If you open it from Self-Service, the simplified view drops some of these, including Resolution Information.
- **Hardware** (alm_hardware.do) has tabs: General, Financial, Contracts and Disposal.

None are recorded for the other two forms:
- **Problem** (problem.do): the notes only mention fields and buttons on the form, such as Problem statement, Configuration item and Mark Duplicate.
- **User** (sys_user.do): the notes describe filling in fields like User ID, name, email and time zone, then clicking Submit.

For these two, the answer rests on no tabs being mentioned, not on a note saying the form has none.

\boxed{three}

I am working with our ServiceNow portal. When marking a problem as duplicate, a popup appears to collect additional information. Which field(s) are actually in that popup? Select ONE.

A. Duplicate of
B. Duplicate of; Resolution code
C. Duplicate of; Resolution code; Close notes
D. Duplicate of; Resolution code; Work notes / internal comments
E. Duplicate of; Resolution code; Customer-facing comments / additional information
F. Duplicate of; Resolution code; Parent
G. Duplicate of; Resolution code; Canonical problem; Notes
H. Duplicate of; Resolution code; Reason for marking as duplicate (short explanation)

Put your final answer into \boxed{} format like \boxed{A}.

results.answer:
The **"Duplicate of"** field is the only one in the popup.

According to the stored notes on the portal, clicking **Mark Duplicate** on a Problem record shows the "Duplicate of" reference field. The system then sets the Resolution code to "Duplicate" and the State to "Closed" by itself, so Resolution code isn't something you fill in.

The notes say the button "displays" the field and don't use the word "popup", so treat this as the best match rather than a confirmed description of the popup.

One related point: if the problem is Priority 1 (Critical), the company's "Problem List Cleanup" protocol also requires you to change its Description to "Duplicate". You do that on the form, not in the popup.

\boxed{A}

target.question: I am working with our ServiceNow portal. My boss asked me to rebalance workload between several agents by reassigning problems with a specific tag. What are the two modules that our company's workflow typically use in order to accomplish this task? Tell me the first module's name and the second module's name in order, separated by a semicolon. Mark your final answer (should be two short phrases separated by a semicolon) in \boxed{}.

results.answer:
The company's "Agent Workload Balancing" protocol (KB0010104) uses two modules, in this order:

1. **Reports** (`sys_report_list.do`): Open the report called "Problems for with hashtag #{hashtag}" and click "View Report". It shows a bar chart of assignee counts, so you can see who has the most problems with the tag and who has the fewest.
2. **Problems** (`problem_list.do`): Filter for "Problem statement contains #{hashtag}" AND "Assigned to is {busiest agent}". Open a matching problem with Priority 5 (Planning). Change "Assigned to" to the agent with the fewest problems and click Update.

The reports are listed under the Reports menu, where there is also a "View / Run" item.

\boxed{Reports; Problems}

| FORK
    ( WHERE content:"rebalance workload reassign problems tag" OR title:"rebalance workload reassign problems tag" OR description:"rebalance workload reassign problems tag" | SORT _score DESC | LIMIT 20 )
    ( WHERE content.semantic:"rebalance workload between agents by reassigning problems with a specific tag modules" OR title.semantic:"rebalance workload reassigning problems tag" OR description.semantic:"rebalance workload reassigning problems tag" | SORT _score DESC | LIMIT 20 )
| FUSE

target.question:
I am working with our ServiceNow portal. My boss asks me to onboard a new user. After creating the new user profile, I navigate to order an Apple Mac Book Pro for this user and complete the order. What step remains? (Select ONE.)

A. Return to the onboarding task -> add the MacBook Request (REQ) / Request Item (RITM) number in Work notes for traceability -> change the task state from Open to Closed - Complete.
B. Navigate back to the onboarding task -> write a brief summary in Additional comments for the hiring manager/requester -> click Close Task (or set state to Closed - Complete).
C. Verify the Request Item (RITM) was successfully created -> link it to the parent onboarding ticket -> then mark the onboarding task as Complete/Closed - Complete to trigger the next workflow phase.
D. Create a new hardware record -> then return to the onboarding task page and change the status/state from Open to Closed - Complete.
E. Return to the new user profile (sys_user) -> confirm the MacBook request is associated with the user/asset context -> validate provisioning details (delivery location/approvals) -> then close the onboarding task as Closed - Complete.
F. Open the created MacBook request -> verify it is submitted and assigned to the correct fulfillment group -> notify the requester/manager with the tracking details -> then close the onboarding task as Closed - Complete.
G. Return to the onboarding task -> reassign/hand off the task to the next fulfillment team -> set the task state to In Progress (so they can continue fulfillment).
H. Create a new hardware record -> open the MacBook request and attach the hardware record -> then send the new user a completion message and close the onboarding task as Closed - Complete.

Put your final answer into \boxed{} format like \boxed{A}.

results.answer:
The answer is D. The AI Index has the company's "Onboarding a new user" protocol, which lists these steps in order:

1. Create the user record in the Users (sys_user) table.
2. Order the requested hardware, such as the Apple MacBook Pro, from the Service Catalog.
3. Create a matching Hardware Asset record with the model and asset tag details.
4. Change the onboarding Private Task's state to "Closed Complete".

You've done steps 1 and 2. What's left is creating the hardware record and then closing the onboarding task. The protocol says plainly that stopping before those steps leaves the onboarding incomplete.

The other options don't fit:
- Option H also creates the hardware record, but it adds steps the protocol doesn't call for: attaching the record to the request and sending the user a message.
- Options A, B, C, E and F skip the hardware record.
- Option G leaves the task In Progress when it should be closed.

\boxed{D}
